title.narrative: Learning and teaching supported in crisis-affected contexts in West Africa

description.narrative: Insecurity, extreme poverty, inequalities, rapid population growth, and climate change continue to drive high levels of vulnerability across West Africa. Escalating violence and insecurity have caused mass displacements, pushing school closures to historic highs with over 14,800 schools shut down in West and Central Africa, directly disrupting the education of more than 3 million children. Being deprived of a safe learning environment inflicts profound, long-term trauma on children and youth, severely impacting their mental health, psychosocial well-being, and physical safety. Beyond the immediate loss of learning, prolonged exclusion from quality education exponentially heightens their exposure to protection risks, including recruitment by armed groups, child labor, physical violence, and sexual exploitation. This educational crisis is further amplified by expanding climate change-induced disasters and impacts, such as heatwaves, flooding and droughts, which physically destroy school infrastructure, displace communities, and repeatedly interrupt school calendars and access. Against this background, UNESCO will support countries in increasing access to quality education and learning opportunities from early childhood to higher education, for vulnerable children and youth living in crisis-affected contexts, and in fostering the resilience of education systems. In the course of last biennium, efforts were undertaken to strengthen the capacities of education actors in formulating strategies for reinforcing the preparedness and response to emergencies and crisis situations of education systems.
